rule_sets.notes: British Columbia College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) Registration Requirements Once you graduate from the Bachelor of Science in Nursing program, you must apply for registration as a Registered Nurse with the BCCNM to be eligible for employment. To register you must meet the BCCNM Competencies and Standards for Entry-Level Registered Nurse Practice in British Columbia. It is important that you are aware of these prior to applying for admission to the Nursing program. These requirements are described on the BCCNM’s Website at the following links: Requisite Skills and Abilities [PDF] New Graduate Competencies [PDF] Professional Nursing Standards Course Requirements Computer with a web camera, microphone and speaker, sufficient RAM and compatible with Respondus Lockdown Browser . Textbooks WiFi / Internet access (available on campus) If you’re a student who requires accommodations due to a disability, then contact BCIT’s Accessibility Services . Scheduled intakes January, April and September each year. Application processing This program is open to applications: January intake: June 1st* to July 15th* April intake: October 1st* to November 15th* September intake: February 1st* to March 15th* *or next business day We recommend that you apply early . All supporting documents must be submitted by the application deadline. Indigenous applicants : Read about Indigenous student support available for the Nursing program. Entrance requirements Competitive Entry: Three-step process Meeting the minimum entrance requirements does not guarantee admission. Admission is competitive, and qualified applicants are assessed and ranked based on the department’s competitive selection criteria. Offers of admission are made to the most competitive applicants based on the available seats for each intake. When the number of qualified applicants exceeds the available seats, the program may establish a waitlist. Waitlisted applicants who are not admitted will be invited to have their application considered for the following intake. Future-intake consideration does not guarantee admission. Step 1: Meet the following entrance requirements English language proficiency: Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Math: one of the following or equivalent: Pre-Calculus 11 (73%) or 12 (67%) or Foundations of Math 11 (73%) or 12 (73%) or MATH 0007 – Technical Mathematics Introduction (73%) Chemistry 11 (73%) or equivalent Academic Foundations: 18.0 post-secondary credits with a minimum of 67% in each of the following courses: ENGL 1177 – Academic Writing or equivalent* (3.0 credits) Note: ENGL 1177 may also be used to satisfy the English language proficiency. BHSC 1200 – Human Anatomy and Physiology or equivalent*, completed within the past three years (6.0 credits) PSYC 1101 – Introductory Psychology 1 or equivalent* (3.0 credits) General Education [PDF] electives at a 100-level minimum in at least two different academic disciplines (6.0 credits) * View acceptable equivalent courses [PDF] Applicants must submit final grades for the listed Academic Foundations courses by the application deadline. In-progress courses are not accepted for this program. Complete the following form for submission with your online application: Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire [PDF] : This form will be used with other entrance requirements in the competitive selection for the program. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. These reports must include course-by-course evaluations and GPA calculations. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Step 2: Department assessment Applicants who meet the minimum entrance requirements will be assessed and ranked competitively. Admission decisions are based on academic achievement and the assessment of the Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire. Preference will be given to applicants who demonstrate: Strong academic achievement in previous post-secondary studies Additional post-secondary education Exposure to healthcare environments, patient care, or community service through employment, volunteer activities, or other experiences Relevant knowledge, skills, experiences, and attributes aligned with the nursing profession Preference may also be given to applicants who were previously waitlisted and highly ranked. Step 3: Conditionally selected applicants If you have been conditionally accepted to BCIT, you will be notified and the following information will be required in order to be accepted into the program: Criminal Record Check [PDF] Immunization Records Complete the Immunization Review Form available on the BCIT Student Health Services website and submit directly to the Student Health Services address on the form. The due date for this form is in your acceptance letter. Contact Student Health Services at 604-432-8843 if you require information regarding immunizations. If you receive immunizations from BCIT Student Health Services, you will need to upload the immunization record, that is emailed to you, to your Health Gateway profile . If you are not able to locate your record, please email nurses@bcit.ca with your name, DOB, and student ID number to request it. You are encouraged to begin these requirements as soon as you accept your offer of admission, as obtaining Criminal Record Check, gathering immunization records, and completing any required follow-up may take time. Once these and any other outstanding conditions have been met, you will receive notification of your full acceptance. Clinical requirements Note: All health care workers who come into contact with patients at publicly funded health care facilities or in the community, including at long-term care facilities, must have the influenza vaccine or wear a mask during flu season. This policy affects all students who will be entering a clinical setting. As such, you will be required to provide proof of your immunization or agree to wear a mask at all times through the flu season prior to being placed in your clinical studies. Face Respirator Fit Testing A face piece respiratory fit test may be required before students are permitted to enter the clinical practicum. Upon successful completion of the fit test, the original certificate must be presented to the program and annual re-fitting is required. Students are expected to carry their certificate with them at all times during their practicum. For the Respirator Fit Testing, fit testing with a N95 respirator (1860, 1860s, or 1870) is required and must be performed, in accordance with CSA Standard CAN/CSA-Z94.4-02. Fit Testing must also include inspection, cleaning, maintenance, and storage of protective equipment. Students will be given specific instructions in preparation for their fit testing by the provider they choose. CPR - BLS (HCP) Current Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) - Basic Life Support for Health Care Providers (HCP). Certificate must be submitted prior to the first day of term 1 and be recertified annually.. Certifications from any of the following agencies are accepted: Lifesaving Society, Red Cross, Heart & Stroke Foundation, St Johns Ambulance, and the Canadian Ski Patrol. International applicants This program is not available to international students. View available programs . Apply to program Note: The January 2027 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for re-admission may still be submitted. Applications for the April 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) is a three-year full-time program, that is delivered in three terms per year. The program is based on a concept, competency-based approach. Students are exposed to the latest technology, innovative practice-based experiences, and provided with a range of resources. Note: The January 2027 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for re-admission may still be submitted. Applications for the April 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. Delivery: in person. See details . Application processing This program is open to applications: January intake: June 1st* to July 15th* April intake: October 1st* to November 15th* September intake: February 1st* to March 15th* *or next business day We recommend that you apply early . Entrance requirements Competitive Entry: Three-step process Meeting the minimum entrance requirements does not guarantee admission. Admission is competitive, and qualified applicants are assessed and ranked based on the department\u2019s competitive selection criteria. Offers of admission are made to the most competitive applicants based on the available seats for each intake. When the number of qualified applicants exceeds the available seats, the program may establish a waitlist. rule_sets.notes: British Columbia College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) Registration Requirements Once you graduate from the Bachelor of Science in Nursing program, you must apply for registration as a Registered Nurse with the BCCNM to be eligible for employment. To register you must meet the BCCNM Competencies and Standards for Entry-Level Registered Nurse Practice in British Columbia. It is important that you are aware of these prior to applying for admission to the Nursing program. These requirements are described on the BCCNM’s Website at the following links: Requisite Skills and Abilities [PDF] New Graduate Competencies [PDF] Professional Nursing Standards Course Requirements Computer with a web camera, microphone and speaker, sufficient RAM and compatible with Respondus Lockdown Browser . Textbooks WiFi / Internet access (available on campus) If you’re a student who requires accommodations due to a disability, then contact BCIT’s Accessibility Services . Scheduled intakes January, April and September each year. Application processing This program is open to applications: January intake: June 1st* to July 15th* April intake: October 1st* to November 15th* September intake: February 1st* to March 15th* *or next business day We recommend that you apply early . All supporting documents must be submitted by the application deadline. Indigenous applicants : Read about Indigenous student support available for the Nursing program. Entrance requirements Competitive Entry: Three-step process Meeting the minimum entrance requirements does not guarantee admission. Admission is competitive, and qualified applicants are assessed and ranked based on the department’s competitive selection criteria. Offers of admission are made to the most competitive applicants based on the available seats for each intake. When the number of qualified applicants exceeds the available seats, the program may establish a waitlist. Waitlisted applicants who are not admitted will be invited to have their application considered for the following intake. Future-intake consideration does not guarantee admission. Step 1: Meet the following entrance requirements English language proficiency: Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Math: one of the following or equivalent: Pre-Calculus 11 (73%) or 12 (67%) or Foundations of Math 11 (73%) or 12 (73%) or MATH 0007 – Technical Mathematics Introduction (73%) Chemistry 11 (73%) or equivalent Academic Foundations: 18.0 post-secondary credits with a minimum of 67% in each of the following courses: ENGL 1177 – Academic Writing or equivalent* (3.0 credits) Note: ENGL 1177 may also be used to satisfy the English language proficiency. BHSC 1200 – Human Anatomy and Physiology or equivalent*, completed within the past three years (6.0 credits) PSYC 1101 – Introductory Psychology 1 or equivalent* (3.0 credits) General Education [PDF] electives at a 100-level minimum in at least two different academic disciplines (6.0 credits) * View acceptable equivalent courses [PDF] Applicants must submit final grades for the listed Academic Foundations courses by the application deadline. In-progress courses are not accepted for this program. Complete the following form for submission with your online application: Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire [PDF] : This form will be used with other entrance requirements in the competitive selection for the program. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. These reports must include course-by-course evaluations and GPA calculations. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Step 2: Department assessment Applicants who meet the minimum entrance requirements will be assessed and ranked competitively. Admission decisions are based on academic achievement and the assessment of the Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire. Preference will be given to applicants who demonstrate: Strong academic achievement in previous post-secondary studies Additional post-secondary education Exposure to healthcare environments, patient care, or community service through employment, volunteer activities, or other experiences Relevant knowledge, skills, experiences, and attributes aligned with the nursing profession Preference may also be given to applicants who were previously waitlisted and highly ranked. Step 3: Conditionally selected applicants If you have been conditionally accepted to BCIT, you will be notified and the following information will be required in order to be accepted into the program: Criminal Record Check [PDF] Immunization Records Complete the Immunization Review Form available on the BCIT Student Health Services website and submit directly to the Student Health Services address on the form. The due date for this form is in your acceptance letter. Contact Student Health Services at 604-432-8843 if you require information regarding immunizations. If you receive immunizations from BCIT Student Health Services, you will need to upload the immunization record, that is emailed to you, to your Health Gateway profile . If you are not able to locate your record, please email nurses@bcit.ca with your name, DOB, and student ID number to request it. You are encouraged to begin these requirements as soon as you accept your offer of admission, as obtaining Criminal Record Check, gathering immunization records, and completing any required follow-up may take time. Once these and any other outstanding conditions have been met, you will receive notification of your full acceptance. program.program_overview: The Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) is a three-year full-time program, that is delivered in three terms per year. The program is based on a concept, competency-based approach. Students are exposed to the latest technology, innovative practice-based experiences, and provided with a range of resources. Note: The January 2027 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for re-admission may still be submitted. Applications for the April 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. Delivery: in person. See details . The BCIT BSN program is committed to preparing excellent nurses who are practice ready to meet the complex care needs in today’s health care environment. About the program Accelerated, three-year, full-time Bachelor of Science in Nursing program Three intakes per year: January, April and September BSN Simulation provides students with hands-on, safe and state-of-the-art experiences to prepare learners for practice Clinical experiences in a variety of acute care settings and community agencies Two specialty nursing courses are included in the degree BCIT Bachelor of Science in Nursing Program Visit Program Details to learn more about our BSN program. Who it’s for This program is for individuals who: Are able to care for the physical and emotional well-being of a variety of patients Have the emotional stability to effectively manage the needs of patients, and to cope in stressful situations Are fluent in written and oral English Are team players, able to work independently, and take initiative while maintaining ethical standards and values Have a strong work ethic and are committed to a heavy course load Are able to work day, night, and weekend shifts in a physically demanding, fast-paced environment Are Canadian residents Thrive in an innovative, technical, and caring environment Are interested in developing problem-solving and critical thinking skills Have good manual dexterity to work with sensitive material and equipment This BSN program is guided by the British Columbia College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) standards. In order to work as an RN, graduates must meet the required competencies and standards set by the College. You can find out more on these sites: Requisite Skills and Abilities Entry-level Competencies Professional Nursing Standards Visit Entrance Requirements to learn more about program entry requirements and registration. rule_sets.notes: British Columbia College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) Registration Requirements Once you graduate from the Bachelor of Science in Nursing program, you must apply for registration as a Registered Nurse with the BCCNM to be eligible for employment. To register you must meet the BCCNM Competencies and Standards for Entry-Level Registered Nurse Practice in British Columbia. It is important that you are aware of these prior to applying for admission to the Nursing program. These requirements are described on the BCCNM’s Website at the following links: Requisite Skills and Abilities [PDF] New Graduate Competencies [PDF] Professional Nursing Standards Course Requirements Computer with a web camera, microphone and speaker, sufficient RAM and compatible with Respondus Lockdown Browser . Textbooks WiFi / Internet access (available on campus) If you’re a student who requires accommodations due to a disability, then contact BCIT’s Accessibility Services . Scheduled intakes January, April and September each year. Application processing This program is open to applications: January intake: June 1st* to July 15th* April intake: October 1st* to November 15th* September intake: February 1st* to March 15th* *or next business day We recommend that you apply early . All supporting documents must be submitted by the application deadline. Indigenous applicants : Read about Indigenous student support available for the Nursing program. Entrance requirements Competitive Entry: Three-step process Meeting the minimum entrance requirements does not guarantee admission. Admission is competitive, and qualified applicants are assessed and ranked based on the department’s competitive selection criteria. Offers of admission are made to the most competitive applicants based on the available seats for each intake. When the number of qualified applicants exceeds the available seats, the program may establish a waitlist. Waitlisted applicants who are not admitted will be invited to have their application considered for the following intake. Future-intake consideration does not guarantee admission. Step 1: Meet the following entrance requirements English language proficiency: Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Math: one of the following or equivalent: Pre-Calculus 11 (73%) or 12 (67%) or Foundations of Math 11 (73%) or 12 (73%) or MATH 0007 – Technical Mathematics Introduction (73%) Chemistry 11 (73%) or equivalent Academic Foundations: 18.0 post-secondary credits with a minimum of 67% in each of the following courses: ENGL 1177 – Academic Writing or equivalent* (3.0 credits) Note: ENGL 1177 may also be used to satisfy the English language proficiency. BHSC 1200 – Human Anatomy and Physiology or equivalent*, completed within the past three years (6.0 credits) PSYC 1101 – Introductory Psychology 1 or equivalent* (3.0 credits) General Education [PDF] electives at a 100-level minimum in at least two different academic disciplines (6.0 credits) * View acceptable equivalent courses [PDF] Applicants must submit final grades for the listed Academic Foundations courses by the application deadline. In-progress courses are not accepted for this program. Complete the following form for submission with your online application: Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire [PDF] : This form will be used with other entrance requirements in the competitive selection for the program. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. These reports must include course-by-course evaluations and GPA calculations. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Step 2: Department assessment Applicants who meet the minimum entrance requirements will be assessed and ranked competitively. Admission decisions are based on academic achievement and the assessment of the Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire. Preference will be given to applicants who demonstrate: Strong academic achievement in previous post-secondary studies Additional post-secondary education Exposure to healthcare environments, patient care, or community service through employment, volunteer activities, or other experiences Relevant knowledge, skills, experiences, and attributes aligned with the nursing profession Preference may also be given to applicants who were previously waitlisted and highly ranked. Step 3: Conditionally selected applicants If you have been conditionally accepted to BCIT, you will be notified and the following information will be required in order to be accepted into the program: Criminal Record Check [PDF] Immunization Records Complete the Immunization Review Form available on the BCIT Student Health Services website and submit directly to the Student Health Services address on the form. The due date for this form is in your acceptance letter. Contact Student Health Services at 604-432-8843 if you require information regarding immunizations. If you receive immunizations from BCIT Student Health Services, you will need to upload the immunization record, that is emailed to you, to your Health Gateway profile . If you are not able to locate your record, please email nurses@bcit.ca with your name, DOB, and student ID number to request it. You are encouraged to begin these requirements as soon as you accept your offer of admission, as obtaining Criminal Record Check, gathering immunization records, and completing any required follow-up may take time. Once these and any other outstanding conditions have been met, you will receive notification of your full acceptance. The BCIT BSN program is committed to preparing excellent nurses who are practice ready to meet the complex care needs in today’s health care environment. About the program Accelerated, three-year, full-time Bachelor of Science in Nursing program Three intakes per year: January, April and September BSN Simulation provides students with hands-on, safe and state-of-the-art experiences to prepare learners for practice Clinical experiences in a variety of acute care settings and community agencies Two specialty nursing courses are included in the degree BCIT Bachelor of Science in Nursing Program Visit Program Details to learn more about our BSN program. Who it’s for This program is for individuals who: Are able to care for the physical and emotional well-being of a variety of patients Have the emotional stability to effectively manage the needs of patients, and to cope in stressful situations Are fluent in written and oral English Are team players, able to work independently, and take initiative while maintaining ethical standards and values Have a strong work ethic and are committed to a heavy course load Are able to work day, night, and weekend shifts in a physically demanding, fast-paced environment Are Canadian residents Thrive in an innovative, technical, and caring environment Are interested in developing problem-solving and critical thinking skills Have good manual dexterity to work with sensitive material and equipment This BSN program is guided by the British Columbia College of Nurses and Midwives (BCCNM) standards. In order to work as an RN, graduates must meet the required competencies and standards set by the College.
